label: 4th original token (t=3) when the sequence starts with digit 2
explanation: Strictly positional: fires only at step t=3 of the original phase (44521 of 44527 activations; 6 at t=4). It never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase, so L=3 sequences (where step 3 is <DEL>) never activate it. It fires on about 9% of t=3 steps, and which ones depends on the first few original tokens. If the first token is the digit 2 it fires about 97% of the time; this case holds 69% of activation mass and nearly all of the top quartile. The strongest activations (about 1.0) come on prefixes like 2 u g. Other prefixes give weaker activations, e.g. first token 3 or l, or second token 2, 3 or u. Prefixes made only of letters like p c b give near-zero activations. The identity of the token at step 3 matters little. Predicate (t=3, L>3, and digit 2 in position 0 or 1) gives dev precision 0.68, recall 0.49, F1 0.57 and mass recall 0.79. Widening the prefix sets raises mass recall to about 0.9 but costs precision. The low-magnitude tail is a diffuse function of the prefix that no simple predicate captures.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: 2, 3, l, o, p, k; least: a, e, s, f) and the second original token (most: 2, 3, u, l, g, i; least: m, z, e, s); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, L=6 & t=3, L=7 & t=3.
